description: Oh no! The shutoff under the sink won't budge, and now it's dripping down your wrist.
option_2: Shut off the main and replace the shutoff
option_3: Crank harder with a pipe wrench

description: You closed the main, but water is still trickling. The main valve has given up on life.
option_1: Replace every valve in the house
option_2: Call the water utility to shut off at the street
option_3: Work fast with a bucket and hope

description: Ugh! The faucet nuts are rusted solid, and you're upside down in the cabinet with a flashlight in your mouth.
option_1: Cut the old faucet out with an oscillating tool
option_2: Pull the whole sink out of the countertop
option_3: Use penetrating oil and a basin wrench

description: Yikes! The old supply line snaps the moment you bend it.
option_1: Reuse the old line very gently

description: Surprise! Your new faucet needs one hole. Your sink has three.
option_2: Cover the extra holes with a deck plate
option_3: Fill the extra holes with caulk

description: Squish. The cabinet floor is soft and smells like a swamp. Years of slow leaks, finally revealed.
option_1: Lay a plastic mat over it
option_3: Cut out and replace the cabinet floor

description: The new sink is one inch too wide for the countertop cutout. Of course it is.
option_1: Return it for a sink that fits
option_2: Force it in with a rubber mallet

description: Hmm. Next to your shiny new faucet, the backsplash looks straight out of 1987.
option_2: Paint over the tile with wall paint
option_3: Add it to the someday list

description: Your partner calls from the hallway: "While you're at it, can you change this bulb?"
option_1: Leave the sink in pieces and do it now
option_2: Install smart lighting throughout the house
option_3: Change it once the faucet is done

description: You cut off the old valve, and now there's barely half an inch of pipe left to grab.
option_1: Use a push-fit valve made for short stubs
option_2: Open the wall and repipe the run

description: The water utility can shut off the street valve... on Monday. It's Friday night.
option_1: Turn the street valve yourself with a broom handle
option_2: Cap the sink lines and wait until Monday
option_3: Hire an emergency plumber to freeze the pipe

description: The oscillating tool slips. There's now a shiny scratch across your stainless sink.

option_3: Buff it out with a scratch repair kit

description: The new supply lines are 3/8 inch. Your valves are 1/2 inch. The hardware store closes in 20 minutes.
option_1: Wrap the threads in tape until it holds
option_2: Grab the right adapters before close
option_3: Buy one of every fitting in the aisle

description: Crack! A chunk of laminate pops off while you're widening the cutout.
option_3: Fill it with a color-matched repair kit

description: Under the rotten cabinet floor: fuzzy black spots. Mold has moved in and stopped paying rent.
option_1: Gut the kitchen to the studs
option_2: Clean, dry, and treat the area
